Hi Helen —

Really glad the demo landed well. I reviewed your usage file and sketched two practical structures that customers use for the exact variability you're describing:

Option A — Banded marginal pricing (recommended for bursty months)
- Commit bands (monthly): 0–2M, 2–8M, 8M+ tokens.
- Marginal discount applied only to the tokens in the higher band.
- Unused commit: option to carry forward up to N% as credits (we usually see 25–35% cap).

Option B — Blended tier (simpler billing)
- One blended per-token rate based on total billed usage vs committed baseline; easier for procurement but can be more expensive for customers with big spikes.

Tradeoffs: marginal preserves upside for you when you spike; blended is easier for internal finance and forecasting. For your flows, marginal + carry-forward credits tends to hit the best unit economics without penalizing burst months.

I attached a working spreadsheet (pricing-band-proposal-v1.xlsx) with example math for both options and a short term-sheet (MCP-term-sheet.pdf) showing standard carry-forward language.

Next steps I suggest:
1) Aditya and I can run your file through three sample scenarios and return exact $/1k-token comparisons.
2) If procurement is happy, we can prepare a DocuSign with a 6-month pilot commit and optional staircase discounts.

Would you prefer we model a 6-month pilot or annual commit? If you share which months you expect spikes, we’ll tailor the band thresholds.

Thanks,

2) Credit expiry: we'd like any carry-forward credits to expire after 3 months. Can you confirm a 90-day expiry?

3) Billing visibility: Jacob asked whether per-route token-level breakdowns can be provided in the invoice/console for reconciliation.

If we can get answers to the above, procurement will be ready to review a DocuSign for a 6-month pilot. We expect the first spike in month 2.

On the blended vs marginal point — procurement leans toward blended for simplicity, but Jacob is open to marginal if the carry-forward logic is automated.

Thanks,

Hi Helen — looping in the calc scenarios and the quick math. I modeled three months that reflect your note (low, spike, recover). Key assumptions in the sheet (calc-scenarios.csv): token counts per month and an 8M/month proposed baseline for the pilot.

Short worked example (numbers are illustrative):
- Commit: 8M tokens/month.
- Band A (0–2M): $0.00120 /1k tokens
- Band B (2–8M): $0.00095 /1k tokens
- Band C (8M+): $0.00070 /1k tokens

Scenario month-by-month (billed tokens):
- Month 1: 4M used => billed = (2M * A) + (2M * B) => blended effective = $0.00108 /1k
- Month 2 (spike): 12M used => billed = (2M*A) + (6M*B) + (4M*C) => marginal advantage on spike tokens
- Month 3: 3M used + 30% carry-forward credits from month 1 applied => net billed usage reduced accordingly

Comparing marginal vs blended for Month 2 shows ~12–18% unit savings on the spike under marginal pricing depending on band widths. The blended approach would average across the quarter and reduce variability but can cost more when spikes are large.

Implementation notes:
- Carry-forward design: automatic application in the billing system is straightforward; we can implement a rolling 90-day window with a 30% cap on monthly commit carried forward.
- Invoice line items: we can include per-band token counts and effective rates for reconciliation.

Attaching calc-scenarios.csv with the numbers and the pricing-band-proposal-v1.xlsx for your procurement review.

If you want I can push these into a quick 1-page appendix that procurement can slot into the DocuSign package.

Cheers,
